question: Analyse how increased media coverage of basketball can positively impact on the standard of a young player's performance. Refer to Bandura's observational learning theory in your answer.
markScheme:
Possible content may include:
AO1 - Knowledge of media coverage: TV/satellite/internet/social media coverage of basketball has increased. Observational learning theory: acceptable and unacceptable behaviour is watched and copied via four stages - Attention (observer attracted to watch), Retention (learner recalls the observed behaviour), Motor reproduction (learner reproduces the behaviour), Motivation (learner encouraged to repeat the behaviour).
AO2 - Application to young basketball players: (Attention) significance of watching top league games, easily accessible via TV/internet and well branded; young players watch role models performing skills/tactics/scoring. (Retention) role models playing for top teams are seen performing skills, reinforced by repeated/shared media coverage and pundit commentary. (Motor reproduction) young players try to emulate the skills/techniques/tactics of their role models. (Motivation) coaches/managers/parents encourage and reward attempts to be skilful, which is copied.
AO3 - Analysis of positive impact: players become more effective at dribbling/passing/shooting/beating an opponent; the standard of the game becomes quicker and more technical; games become more entertaining for spectators; young players develop technical aspects earlier, accelerating development; the pathway into senior basketball is supported by the increase in skill. However, players may try to copy skills beyond their capability, causing loss of possession, or focus too much on the observed skills and neglect other components of performance.
Accept any other appropriate analysis of how increased media coverage of basketball has positively impacted on the standard of young players' performances.
Max 8 marks.

question:
Income from commercialisation has made an impact on sport.
The table below shows the estimated income from broadcasting rights for a professional rugby league competition over a 20-year period.
Period | Broadcasting income
1996-2000 | £12 million
2001-2005 | £28 million
2006-2010 | £65 million
2011-2015 | £140 million
2016-2020 | £210 million
Evaluate the impact of commercialisation on the professional rugby league competition since 1996. Refer to the table above in your response.
markScheme:
Possible content may include:
AO1 - Knowledge of increased commercialisation: commercialisation is treating sport as a commodity/using it as an asset to be sold; involves sponsorship and media coverage; characterised by professional sport, entertainment, contracts, athletes as commodities, focus on results.
AO2 - Application: broadcasting income has risen sharply over the period shown, from £12 million to £210 million; investment from broadcasters to show live matches; the competition has become a global brand shown in many countries; sponsorship of kits/stadia/competition naming rights.
AO3 - Evaluation. Positive impacts: increased revenue/investment allows higher wages, attracting the best players; increased income has led to improved facilities, coaching, training and rehabilitation, raising the standard of the sport; officials can train full-time and benefit from improved decision-making technology; money raised benefits grass-roots opportunities. Negative impacts: income is not distributed evenly between clubs, creating inequality; global appeal leads to intense media scrutiny of any indiscretion; control of decision making increasingly rests with a small group of wealthy individuals/companies; fixture timings dictated by broadcasters; increases likelihood of gamesmanship/win-at-all-costs attitude, reducing the sport's traditional appeal.
Accept other appropriate evaluation of the impact of commercialisation.
Max 8 marks.

question:
A leading professional basketball player recently became the highest earner in their domestic league, with a reported salary considerably higher than that of any teammate.
Evaluate the impact that wages associated with modern day professionalism in basketball has on the status and motivation of players.
markScheme:
Possible content may include:
AO1 - Knowledge of modern day professionalism and motivation: the modern professional is respected for their talent, has more time to train, experiences celebrity status and can be a positive role model. Motivation can be intrinsic or extrinsic, with extrinsic being tangible or intangible.
AO2 - Application to basketball: status influences a player's ability to become a role model and their responsibilities may increase; higher-status players may access better facilities and opportunities; status may lead to charity work/public speaking opportunities; status may attract sponsorship/commercial/media attention; players receive high monetary rewards for their talent; more money is invested in the sport due to professionalism; professionals train full-time using state-of-the-art facilities; some players are intrinsically motivated by love of the game, others extrinsically motivated by tangible rewards (wages/trophies) or intangible rewards (praise from coaches/fans).
AO3 - Evaluation: increased wages could increase intrinsic motivation to train harder, raising future value and demand, and making for a more entertaining game. Conversely, players may become overly reliant on extrinsic rewards and lose intrinsic motivation, which could be detrimental. Some players may be content to warm the bench while still earning large salaries, losing love for the game and showing little loyalty while chasing higher wages. A balance between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation would be ideal, but over-reliance on the extrinsic could damage intrinsic motives. Higher wages may distract from training/performance as focus shifts to sponsorship/media. Some professionals are motivated to use their status to support charitable work or influence positive change.
Accept any other appropriate evaluation.
Max 8 marks.

question: Explain two benefits of sponsorship to companies investing large amounts of money into sport.
markScheme:
Award a maximum of two AO1 marks and two AO2 marks.
- Increase in publicity/media coverage (1) resulting in increased sales/profit (1)
- Linking the company to an elite athlete (1) adds value to a brand/creates an association with excellence or a healthy image (1)
- Decreases tax paid by the company (1) due to tax relief afforded on money donated as sponsorship (1)
- Being linked to a successful sport/performer (1) can improve the morale of the company's staff (1)
- The company is provided with tickets etc (1) which allows them to build relationships with customers and clients (1)
Answer must include a benefit (AO1) and an explanation of the impact on the company (AO2) to be awarded 2 marks.
Accept other appropriate explanations.
Max 4 marks.

question: Discuss the impact of commercialisation on officials.
markScheme:
Award one mark for each of the following points.
Positive impacts (sub max 2 marks):
- Increased profile/fame which increases awareness and the need for officials to support fair play in sport (1)
- Increase in salary/paid more money and so could become a full-time profession/career pathway (1)
- Increased funding into the sport means more money can be invested into supporting technologies to allow officials to make better/more accurate decisions (1)
- Increased funding can lead to greater support of a network of officials and so greater training (1)
Negative impacts (sub max 2 marks):
- Due to increased coverage of the sport there is increased pressure on officials to make the right decisions (1)
- Criticism of bad performance/could lose their job/reputation damaged if a wrong decision is made (1)
- Officials could become dependent on developed technology so are not confident of making decisions without it (1)
Accept other appropriate discussions.
Max 4 marks.

question:
The media has influenced the nature and extent of mass spectator sport since the nineteenth century.
Explain the advantages of media coverage to a sport and the disadvantages it can have for an elite performer.
markScheme:
7 marks for 7 of: sub max of 4 per section
Advantages to sport:
- Brings in extra funding, eg TV rights, for facilities/equipment/coaches or equivalent ('funding' too vague on its own, needs an impact on use of funding)
- More competitions/extended seasons
- Raises profile of a sport
- Raises participation
- Public educated and informed about the sport
- Provides role models
- Gradually covered more opportunities for female/disabled sport
Disadvantages to performer:
- Control by sponsors/media companies, eg performing when injured/having to use certain brands' equipment/withdrawal of sponsorship
- Extended seasons/player burnout
- Ethical issues - may not agree with company products, eg tobacco
- May have to change image/personality
- Can lead to deviancy to gain extensive material rewards
- Lose traditional values of sport, eg process rather than outcome/loss of respect for opposition
- Privacy issues
- Some sports get more funding/support than others
- Elite female and disabled athletes get fewer opportunities/focus on appearance rather than skill
- Open to criticism from pundits/unrealistic expectations of performance
Max 7 marks.

question:
Many elite sports are now commercialised and seen as a form of entertainment.
Discuss the suggestion that an increase in the commercialisation of sport has been beneficial for performers and the sport.
markScheme:
Possible content may include:
AO1 - Knowledge: identify the beneficial impact of commercialisation using simple statements, eg increase in wages/increase in exposure to the general public.
AO2 - Application: identify and explain the impact, eg increased wages mean performers can train full-time, improving performance; performers become role models, attracting more youngsters and increasing participation.
AO3 - Evaluation: linked explanations/discussion, eg increased wages allow full-time training but may tempt performers to take deviant means (such as doping) to protect their earning power; becoming role models attracts participation but requires performers to maintain a positive public image, and poor behaviour under the spotlight can reduce participation and spectator levels.
Credit other relevant points.
Max 8 marks.

question: Explain why an elite performer should consider the nature of a sponsor and their products before accepting a sponsorship deal.
markScheme:
3 marks for 3 of:
- The performer is a role model for others
- Sport performers therefore have a social duty to others/human rights/unethical manufacturing of goods
- Commercial support depends upon the image of the performer
- Linking to a product that does not reflect the nature of sport/healthy lifestyles, eg links to tobacco/alcohol/junk food companies
- May endanger future commercial support
- Bring criticism to the performer/bad reputation
- Benefits one sponsor will bring compared to another, eg level of income/publicity
- Level of control exerted by sponsor/commitment/expectation, eg public appearances or equivalent
Max 3 marks.

question:
UK Sport distributes a significant amount of funding to selected sports each cycle.
The table below illustrates a fictional funding allocation to different sports in the lead-up to two consecutive Olympic Games.
Sport | Funding for Games A | Funding for Games B | Change of funding
Athletics | £24 100 000 | £26 850 000 | Increase
Sailing | £18 300 000 | £21 600 000 | Increase
Diving | £4 200 000 | £3 150 000 | Decrease
Table tennis | £1 850 000 | £420 000 | Decrease
Water polo | £1 620 000 | No funding | Decrease
Discuss the suggestion that funding should be equal for all sports and not based on performance at major championships.
markScheme:
4 marks for 4 of; sub max of 3 marks
Agree:
- All sports need funding for development/increase chance of success/fair funding (must be clear which perspective is being discussed)
- Helps to promote less familiar/popular sports
- Widens the foundation/participation pyramid/increases grass roots participation
- Provides alternative options for participation/everyone has the right to develop their potential in their chosen sport
- Olympic legacy should be encouraged
Disagree:
- Limited funds have to be used effectively/not enough funding for all sports
- Better to increase chances of winning medals in target sports/tax payers need value for money/no-compromise approach appears to be successful/reward successful sports
- Encourages sports to invest money correctly/accountability/encourages high quality Whole Sport Plans/administrators or equivalent
- Encourages sporting organisations/governing bodies to work together/share resources
- Funding is a privilege not a right
Max 4 marks.

question:
Broadcasters currently pay several billion pounds combined for the media rights to a top domestic football league.
Outline the disadvantages to a sport of increased media control.
markScheme:
4 marks for 4 of:
- Traditional nature of the sport changes/new competitions/formats introduced/rules/regulations/scoring systems altered/clothing/uniforms changed/breaks in play
- Playing times altered/playing seasons altered
- Location of events may be influenced by commercial considerations
- Ticket allocations given to sponsors not fans
- More popular sports gain more coverage at the expense of minority sports
- Media can direct public opinion/support about a sport or event/over-sensationalise negative events, eg deviancy
- Fewer viewers for some sports due to pay-per-view/subscription channels

- Over-saturation on television/spectators become bored with too much sport
Focus of question is on sport, not on teams or individual players.
Max 4 marks.

question: Discuss the suggestion that the increased media coverage of elite sport has had a positive impact on coaches.
markScheme:
Agree (sub max of 2 marks per section):
- Greater profile/public awareness of their role
- Increased salary/job opportunities
- Greater funding from media rights to develop players/team/squad/support systems (not just 'more money' - need to say how it can be used)

- Learn from other coaches
Disagree:

- Greater expectation to deal with media/answer questions/invasion of privacy or equivalent

question:
Sponsorship and commercialisation are an integral part of elite sport.
Evaluate the impact that sponsorship and commercialisation have had on the nature of the sporting experience for the spectator.
markScheme:
Possible content may include:
AO1 - Knowledge: sponsorship is the provision of funds/support for a commercial return, usually a form of advertising; commercialisation is treating sport as a commodity, involving the buying and selling of assets, with the market driving sport.
AO2 - Application to spectators: sponsorship/commercialisation bring money into sport; money means higher standard players/teams and increased excitement watching role models; better/bigger facilities and stadia; team merchandise creates loyalty; money buys technology to make spectating more immersive/interactive; increased number of competitions/opportunities to watch; funding provides an entertaining experience beyond the event itself, eg expert analysis; funding for improved technology at the ground/at home, eg HD/interactive coverage.
AO3 - Analysis of impact: variations of sport format provide alternative viewing experiences; rules changed to create extra excitement; money used for better officiating/technology such as video review, increasing excitement waiting for correct decisions; traditional nature of the sport changed, eg kick-off times arranged to maximise viewing figures; breaks in play for adverts; fewer tickets available for ordinary fans, allocated to sponsors/hospitality, or higher ticket prices; minority sports receive less coverage as major sports dominate schedules; pay-per-view restricts access; companies create a monopoly of merchandise/catering, with expensive merchandise changed regularly.
Accept any other appropriate evaluation.
Max 8 marks.

question:
Many elite sports are now commercialised and seen as a form of entertainment.
Analyse the suggestion that an increase in the 'commercialisation' of sport has been beneficial for performers and the sport.
markScheme:
Possible content may include:
AO1 - Knowledge of commercialisation: treating sport as a commodity; involves the buying and selling of assets with the market as the driving force; elite sport involves professional performers who need income; income depends on the number of spectators/viewers; need to make elite sport a spectacle.
AO2 - Application: increase in wages/prize money/extrinsic rewards/increased sponsorship/professional contracts; performers become well known/role models; increased participation/increased spectators; money provides better facilities/equipment/training support/coaches; performers able to train full-time; money to fund talent identification programmes; money for improved technology at events to aid officials; increase in number of events/competitions; sports become more popular, increasing income further.
AO3 - Analysis: increased income to a sport does not guarantee success; not all sports benefit, money mainly goes to popular sports; sport can lose control of the organisation of events as corporate hospitality takes tickets; over-reliance on money as income, especially TV money, can reduce the need for spectators; rules/formats altered, or sports forced to turn professional; greater pressure/expectation on performers to win; increase in deviant behaviour/cheating/doping/violent play.
Accept any other appropriate analysis.
Max 8 marks.

question:
A leading professional tennis player is one of the most followed athletes on social media. In a recent year they became the first athlete on a major platform to pass 60 million followers.
Discuss the impact this exposure could have upon professional athletes.
markScheme:
Sub-max 2 Advantages:
- Social media allows the athlete to reach a broad and worldwide audience, allowing them to make more money through sponsorship/endorsements (1)
- Social media can bring an athlete in touch with their fans, increasing their fan base/followers (1)
- Social media can further promote the athlete as a brand and image, supporting further career opportunities (1)
Sub-max 2 Disadvantages:
- Social media may expose negative aspects of the athlete's private life, meaning their public image is tarnished (1)
- Social media may provide an opportunity for the public to criticise the athlete's performance, decreasing confidence/drive/motivation to train or play (1)
- Inappropriate comments made by a player on social media become public very quickly and may hinder career prospects (1)
Accept any other appropriate discussion point.
Max 3 marks.
